headline: Direct conversions are up about 6x (about 10 to 62-66 per week) with no spend change, and self-reports point to AI assistants, so no paid channel should get credit; LinkedIn CPA is up 45% and is trimmed 20%.

moves.reason: CPA last 3 wks $282.6 vs $195.6 earlier (+45%) on flat spend (-6%); flag F1 level shift $150->$248 since 8/28. Last-touch ROAS 0.89 and time-decay 1.34 are below the 1.5 target, but first-touch 1.9, Markov 1.83 and linear 1.53 are above, so no full cut. Trim 20% and test.

tests.hypothesis: LinkedIn's true incremental ROAS is above the 1.5 target (as first-touch/Markov/linear imply), and the CPA rise since 8/28 is not just lost incremental value.
tests.design: Geo or audience holdout: suppress LinkedIn for a random 50% of target accounts or regions for 4 weeks while keeping the rest at the trimmed $240/day. Measure total conversions and revenue (all channels including direct and email) in held-out versus exposed groups. Pause LinkedIn if lift is under the 1.5 ROAS break-even.

flag_verdicts.reason: LinkedIn CPA $282.6 over the last 3 weeks vs $195.6 earlier (+45%) on flat spend. Trimmed 20% ($300 to $240/day) and holdout test recommended. Not paused, because 3 of 5 models put ROAS above the 1.5 target.

Google spend spike on 9/12-9/18 (weekly spend $5.2k and $6.7k vs about $4.1k baseline) lifted CPA to about $21-22. It has since reverted: last 3 weeks CPA is $14.51 and ROAS is 12-13. Efficiency is better than before the spike.

Direct rose from 10-15 per week in August to 59-66 per week in the last 3 weeks, with zero paid-spend change. Self-reported 'Asked ChatGPT' went from 0.9% to 19.3% in the latest week, and 'AI assistant' from 0% to 5-8%. The buyers are most likely AI-driven and untracked. I credited no paid channel and moved no budget on it.

flags.message: linkedin CPA rose 1.7x, from $150 to $248, starting 2026-08-28.
google_search spend jumped for 7 days (2026-09-12 to 2026-09-18); CPA rose to $24 from $17.
Direct conversions grew 5.8x (1.6 to 9.3/day) while paid spend moved 1.00x. Self-reported AI answers went from 6% to 20%. Something untracked is driving buyers.
